validator: draft 1 passes validate.mjs with no problems, soft points or warnings. The faults below are the critic's, not the validator's.
keep: The idea is named up front and the rule is in words: the arm's length sets the peak, its turns a second the waves a second, its starting angle where the wave starts.
The causal step from circle to wave is given, not asserted: steady turning makes equal steps of time equal steps of angle, so height against time has the shape of sin θ against angle.

The picture is the brief's: lesson 3's arm on the left, its height carried across by a dashed line and traced against time, with sliders for length, speed (ω beside it) and start angle, a pause, and a switch for the across shadow (projection sources [1][4]; Moore's keystone, notes 6.1).
ω = 2πf is built from lesson 5 (one turn is 2π radians), and E sin(ωt) = E sin(2πft) is cited [3]; 50 Hz is cited [5] and 314.16 rad/s, 20 ms and 5 ms are computed.

The brief's catches each have a DO screen with its own wrong answer: sine read across (screen 2, −1; screen 4, 3.46), period read as frequency (screen 6), f and ω mixed or the 2π lost (screens 8 and 14), the sign of a phase (screen 10), radian mode on 10 sin 100πt (screen 12, 751.5 ms), the second time in a cycle (screens 11 and 12).
The tangent's graph has its one screen (brief, lesson 6), from lesson 3's tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ.
Fifteen screens alternate SHOW 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 with DO 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, closing on two mixed puzzles.
fix: Causal step skipped: 'Every height arrives φ ÷ ω seconds sooner' gives the size of the shift without the reason. Say that the first arm needs φ ÷ ω seconds to turn through φ at ω radians a second, which is the head start the second arm has.

False absolute: 'a level line meets each wave twice' (practice, and screen 11) fails at the peaks, where it touches once, and beyond them, where it never meets. Say a level line between the peaks meets each wave twice.
Qualifier dropped: the note says UK low-voltage supplies are declared at 50 hertz 'unless otherwise agreed in writing'. Keep it, in explain and in the worked example.

Text about the idea, not teaching it: the opening 'An AC supply's wave is drawn by a turning arm' says a mechanism exists that the lesson does not show. Open on what the arm's height draws, and say the AC supply has that shape.
Thin footnoting: 'one turn is 2π radians' is a fact research covers [13] but is unfootnoted. Cite it.

Unreadable at 340 px: screen 13's tangent climbs without limit, so a plot would run off the graph. Clip it at ±4 with small arrows, and give the half-turn repeat its reason (half a turn on, both shadows change sign, so their ratio is the same).

Weak slip wording: screen 8's '100 (the π dropped but not the 2)' names no slip anyone makes. Call it the 100 read off as the frequency, forgetting the 2 in 2π. Screen 11 also needs the reason for dividing by ω (angle = ωt, so t = angle ÷ ω).
Analogy slip: 'level with the axle half-way round' is wrong from the top, where half-way round is the bottom. Say level with the axle at the front and at the back.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with these eight fixes; the screens and numbers keep their order.
